# Playbook: javascript-vanilla-ninja

This playbook holds everything the `javascript-vanilla-ninja` agent applies. When you use it without the agent, work as the role below, apply every rule as binding, and check the result against the acceptance criteria before you finish.

## Role

Principal Frontend Engineer specializing in vanilla ES2023+ JavaScript and Web Platform APIs, accountable for enterprise-grade framework-less code that is modular, secure, performant, and tested.

## Objective

Produce framework-free frontend code built on native ES Modules and standard browser APIs (DOM, Fetch, EventTarget, Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, Observers, Web Workers) that is modular (single-responsibility modules, dependencies injected via factories, no global state), secure by construction against DOM XSS, prototype pollution, and `postMessage` abuse, smooth (no avoidable forced reflows or long tasks on the main thread), free of memory leaks across the entire lifecycle of views and components, robust in asynchronous flows (cancellation, timeouts, retries, no race conditions), and covered by deterministic Vitest tests; the code is type-checked with `// @ts-check` + JSDoc and complies with the project's ESLint flat config, with Vite used only as an optional bundler. Before producing code, apply every rule in the Rules section below as binding, and use the examples in `references/` as the style reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npx eslint .` and `npx tsc -p jsconfig.json` complete with no errors; every file in `src/` starts with `// @ts-check` and uses named exports only.
- No `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with untrusted data, no `eval`/`new Function`/string-based timers; every dynamic URL goes through `new URL()` with a protocol allowlist, and rich HTML goes only through DOMPurify.
- No global variables and no assignments to `window.*`/`globalThis.*`; I/O dependencies (fetch, storage, clock, id generators) are injected and wired exclusively in the `src/main.js` composition root.
- Every view or component has a verifiable cleanup (`destroy()` or `disconnectedCallback`) that removes listeners via `AbortController`, stops timers, calls `disconnect()` on observers, and aborts in-flight fetches.
- Every `fetch` has a timeout and cancellation via `AbortSignal`, there are no floating promises, and a stale response never updates the DOM.
- Lists and DOM updates use event delegation, batched insertions (`DocumentFragment`, `replaceChildren()`), and no interleaved layout reads/writes; CPU-bound computations over 50 ms run in a Web Worker.
- `npx vitest run --coverage` passes with thresholds of at least 80% for lines, functions, and statements and 75% for branches; tests use role-based queries, fake timers for time, and network mocks restored after each test.

## Rules

One section per topic. Each section ends with a pointer to its examples in `references/`.

### 1. Modular JavaScript Architecture with Native ES Modules (`js-modular-architecture`)

*Scope:* Modular architecture for vanilla JavaScript with native ES Modules: feature-based structure, factory-based dependency injection, pure functions, EventTarget stores, typed event bus, import maps, and JSDoc with @ts-check. Use it when creating or reorganizing modules, state, or dependencies.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Organize code by feature: `src/features/<feature>/` contains `<feature>-store.js`, `<feature>-service.js`, `<feature>-view.js`, `types.js`, and an `index.js` that exposes the public API; cross-cutting code lives in `src/shared/`; a feature imports another feature only through its `index.js`, never from its internal files.
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Keep three layers with one-way dependencies: domain (pure functions, no access to the DOM, `fetch`, or storage) ← service/adapter (I/O) ← view (DOM); the domain never imports from service or view, and the service never imports from the view.
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** A single composition root (`src/main.js`) instantiates services, stores, the event bus, and views and wires them together; it is the only module that knows the concrete implementations (`fetch`, `localStorage`, `crypto.randomUUID()`, `new Date()`).
- **[MANDATORY]** Use native ES Modules only: `<script type="module">`, `"type": "module"` in `package.json`, relative specifiers with an explicit extension (`./cart-store.js`); `require()`, IIFEs, and global namespaces (`var App = App || {}`) are forbidden.
- **[MANDATORY]** Use named exports only (`export function`, `export const`, `export class`) to keep import names consistent and renames safe; `export default` is allowed only in tool configuration files that require it (`vite.config.js`, `vitest.config.js`, `eslint.config.js`).
- **[MANDATORY]** Every file in `src/` starts with `// @ts-check`; `jsconfig.json` sets `"checkJs": true`, `"strict": true`, `"noEmit": true`, `"module": "ESNext"`, `"moduleResolution": "Bundler"`, `"target": "ES2023"`, `"lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]`, and CI runs `npx tsc -p jsconfig.json`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Define domain types with `@typedef`/`@property` in the feature's `types.js` and import them with `/** @typedef {import('./types.js').CartItem} CartItem */` or with the `/** @import { CartItem } from './types.js' */` tag (TypeScript 5.5+); every exported function has `@param` and, when not obvious, `@returns`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Sharing state through global variables, `window.App = app`, `globalThis.store = store`, or mutable `export let` (the live binding can be changed by the module and observed everywhere without notification): state lives in instances created by the composition root.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Circular dependencies between modules: block them with the `import-x/no-cycle` rule from `eslint-plugin-import-x` or with `npx madge --circular src/`; a cycle signals a responsibility that must be extracted into a third module.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Side effects at import time (DOM queries, `addEventListener`, `fetch`, timers executed at top level): a module exports only declarations and execution starts from the composition root, so it stays testable and tree-shakeable.
- **[PATTERN]** Dependency injection via factories: `createOrderService({ fetchFn, baseUrl, now, generateId })` receives every I/O dependency as a parameter; importing I/O singletons (`apiClient`, `toast`, `storage`) directly inside the logic is forbidden.
- **[PATTERN]** Domain logic as pure, deterministic functions: no mutation of arguments (spread, `structuredClone()`, ES2023 methods `toSorted()`, `toReversed()`, `toSpliced()`, `with()`), time and randomness injected as `now()`/`random()`, never direct `Date.now()` or `Math.random()` in the domain.
- **[PATTERN]** Observable store: a class that extends `EventTarget` with state in the private field `#state`, `getState()` returning a snapshot frozen with `Object.freeze()`, `dispatch(action)` applying a pure reducer and notifying with `new CustomEvent('change', { detail })` only if the state reference changed, and `subscribe()` returning the unsubscribe function.
- **[PATTERN]** Typed event bus: an `@typedef {{ 'cart:item-added': { productId: string, qty: number } }} AppEventMap` map and generic `emit`/`on` methods with `@template {keyof AppEventMap} K`; event names follow `domain:action`; `on()` accepts `{ signal }` and returns an unsubscribe; the bus is an injected instance backed by a private `EventTarget`, never custom events on `document`.
- **[PATTERN]** One module, one responsibility: catch-all `utils.js`/`helpers.js` files are forbidden; enforce `max-lines: ['warn', 300]` per file and `max-lines-per-function: ['warn', 60]` in ESLint.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Without a bundler, use a single import map (`<script type="importmap">`) declared before any `<script type="module">` to map bare specifiers (`"dompurify": "/vendor/purify.es.mjs"`); supported in Chrome 89+, Firefox 108+, Safari 16.4+. With Vite, use `resolve.alias` in `vite.config.js` and no import map.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** ESLint flat config `eslint.config.js` with `js.configs.recommended`, `languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: 'latest', sourceType: 'module', globals: globals.browser }`, and the rules `no-var`, `prefer-const`, `eqeqeq`, `import-x/no-cycle`, and `no-restricted-syntax` on the selector `AssignmentExpression[left.object.name=/^(window|globalThis)$/]`.
- **[SECURITY]** Freeze shared constants and configuration with `Object.freeze()`; the store exposes only snapshots, never the mutable internal reference; no secrets in client code (`import.meta.env.VITE_*` variables end up in plain text in the public bundle).
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Load non-critical features with dynamic `import()` from the composition root (on first click, on navigation, or when the container enters the viewport) to keep the entry module small; with Vite, every `import()` produces a separate chunk.
- **[TESTING]** Test the domain in the `node` environment with no DOM and no mocks; services and views receive fakes through factory parameters (`fetchFn: vi.fn()`, `now: () => new Date('2025-01-01T00:00:00Z')`) instead of `vi.mock()` on modules.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-modular-architecture.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 2. DOM and Main Thread Performance (`js-dom-performance`)

*Scope:* DOM performance in vanilla JavaScript: event delegation, reads/writes without layout thrashing, requestAnimationFrame, DocumentFragment and templates, passive listeners, IntersectionObserver, debounce, content-visibility, Web Workers, and import(). Use it for lists, scrolling, animations, and jank.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Separate state from rendering: state changes mark the view as dirty and a single `requestAnimationFrame` callback applies all DOM writes for the frame; never one DOM manipulation per event or per modified element.
- **[MANDATORY]** Use event delegation for lists, tables, and menus: a single listener on the container resolves the target with `event.target.closest('[data-action]')` and checks `container.contains(match)`; registering one listener per row or per cell is forbidden.
- **[MANDATORY]** Within the same frame, perform all layout reads first (`getBoundingClientRect()`, `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight`, `clientWidth`, `scrollTop`, `getComputedStyle()`) and only then all writes (`style`, `classList`, node insertions and removals).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Interleaving layout writes and reads in a loop (`el.style.height = 'auto'; el.offsetHeight`): every read after a write forces a synchronous layout, flagged by the DevTools Performance panel as "Forced reflow".
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `innerHTML +=` or `appendChild()` in a loop on an already connected node: the former reparses and recreates the entire content on every iteration (O(n²) cost and lost listeners), the latter invalidates style and layout on every insertion.
- **[PATTERN]** Build multiple insertions off-document in a `DocumentFragment` and apply them with a single `container.append(fragment)` or `container.replaceChildren(...nodes)` call.
- **[PATTERN]** Define repeated markup in a `<template>` and instantiate it with `template.content.cloneNode(true)`, populating fields with `textContent`, `dataset`, and properties: HTML parsing happens only once.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Register `touchstart`, `touchmove`, and `wheel` listeners with `{ passive: true }` when they do not call `preventDefault()`, so scrolling does not wait for the main thread; use `{ passive: false }` only where blocking is essential (custom drag or pinch).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `scroll` handlers that compute visibility with `getBoundingClientRect()` for lazy loading, infinite scroll, analytics impressions, or sticky headers: use `IntersectionObserver` with `rootMargin` (e.g. `'0px 0px 400px 0px'`) and `threshold`, calling `unobserve()` when the target is no longer needed.
- **[PATTERN]** Images with `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, and explicit `width`/`height` to prevent layout shift; no JavaScript lazy-loading libraries for images.
- **[PATTERN]** Debounce search inputs and expensive validations by 250-300 ms; throttle `scroll`, `pointermove`, and `resize` to the frame with `requestAnimationFrame`; observe element dimensions with `ResizeObserver` instead of `window.addEventListener('resize')`.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Give long off-viewport sections `content-visibility: auto` and `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 500px` to skip their layout and paint (Chrome 85+, Firefox 125+, Safari 18+); for lists beyond roughly 1,000 rows use virtualization (render only the visible rows plus a buffer).
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Animate only `transform` and `opacity`, handled by the compositor, via CSS transitions or `element.animate()`; animating `top`, `left`, `width`, `height`, or `margin` is forbidden; apply `will-change` only for the duration of the animation.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** No main-thread task over 50 ms: run CPU-bound computations (parsing large CSV/JSON, filtering and sorting over 10,000 records, diffing, compression) in a Web Worker `new Worker(new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`, transferring `ArrayBuffer`s in the `postMessage` transfer list.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Split long but divisible main-thread work into chunks, yielding control with `scheduler.yield()` (Chromium 129+, not universally supported) with an `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))` fallback.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Load non-critical code (editors, charts, complex modals) with dynamic `import()` on interaction or visibility; preload critical-path modules with `<link rel="modulepreload" href="/src/main.js">`.
- **[SECURITY]** Optimizations must not introduce dangerous sinks: templates and fragments are populated with `textContent` and `setAttribute()`, never by interpolating data into HTML strings "to go faster".
- **[TESTING]** Measure before and after every optimization: Chrome DevTools Performance panel (long tasks, forced reflows, layout shifts), `PerformanceObserver` with `type: 'long-animation-frame'` (Chrome 123+) or `'longtask'`, Core Web Vitals targets INP < 200 ms and CLS < 0.1.
- **[TESTING]** Test debounce, throttle, and schedulers with `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout', 'requestAnimationFrame', 'cancelAnimationFrame'] })` and `vi.advanceTimersByTime()`, with no real waits.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** With Vite, keep `build.modulePreload` enabled (default), analyze chunks with `rollup-plugin-visualizer`, and define a budget for initial JavaScript (e.g. 100 KB gzip) enforced in CI with `size-limit`.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-dom-performance.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 3. Asynchrony, Cancellation, and Concurrency (`js-async-concurrency`)

*Scope:* Asynchrony and concurrency in vanilla JavaScript: async/await, Promise.all vs allSettled, AbortController and AbortSignal.timeout, latest wins, retry with backoff and jitter, Error cause, unhandledrejection, and concurrency pools. Use it for fetches, searches, polling, and uploads.

- **[MANDATORY]** Use `async`/`await` with `try/catch` at the point where the error can actually be handled (UI or feature boundary); nested `.then()` chains and mixing `await` with `.then()` in the same function are forbidden.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Floating promises: every Promise is awaited with `await`, returned to the caller, or terminated with `.catch()`; intentional fire-and-forget is written as `void task().catch(reportError)` (global `reportError()`: Chrome 95+, Firefox 93+, Safari 15.4+).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `items.forEach(async (item) => { await save(item); })` and async callbacks passed to APIs that ignore the returned Promise: use `for...of` with `await` for sequential execution or `Promise.all(array.map(fn))` for parallel execution.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Async executors `new Promise(async (resolve) => resolve(await load()))` (thrown exceptions are lost) and `throw 'string'` or `reject('string')`: always throw `Error` instances, with a stack trace.
- **[PATTERN]** Choose the combinator by semantics: `Promise.all` when you need every result (fail-fast), `Promise.allSettled` when partial results are useful (dashboard widgets, multiple submissions), iterating on `status === 'fulfilled'`/`'rejected'`, `Promise.any` for the first success, `Promise.race` only paired with cancellation of the losing operations.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Start independent operations in parallel with `const [user, orders] = await Promise.all([getUser(signal), getOrders(signal)])` instead of sequential `await`s; never create a promise and leave it waiting for a later `await`, because an early rejection becomes an `unhandledrejection`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Every `fetch` has a timeout and cancellation: `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` (Chrome 103+, Firefox 100+, Safari 16+) combined with the caller's signal via `AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(8000)])` (Chrome 116+, Firefox 124+, Safari 17.4+; for older browsers, fall back to `AbortController` and `setTimeout`).
- **[MANDATORY]** Classify errors: `DOMException` with `name === 'AbortError'` (intentional cancellation: ignore it with no logging and no UI message), `name === 'TimeoutError'` (from `AbortSignal.timeout()`: timeout message, retry allowed), `TypeError` (network error), `!response.ok` (fetch does not reject on 4xx/5xx: throw an `HttpError` with `status`).
- **[PATTERN]** Latest-wins race condition handling for searches, filters, and navigation: on every new request call `abort()` on the previous controller and apply to the DOM only the response of the current request, comparing the controller or an incremental `requestId`.
- **[PATTERN]** Deduplicate identical in-flight requests with a `Map<string, Promise>` (single-flight), removing the key in `finally`, so multiple components requesting the same resource share a single fetch.
- **[PATTERN]** Retry only on transient errors (network, timeout, HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and on idempotent requests (GET, PUT, DELETE, or POST with an `Idempotency-Key` header); exponential backoff with full jitter `Math.random() * Math.min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2 ** attempt)`, at most 3-5 attempts, honor the `Retry-After` header, and make the wait interruptible by the `signal`.
- **[PATTERN]** Enrich errors without losing the original: `throw new Error('Failed to load orders', { cause: error })` (ES2022); domain errors such as `class HttpError extends Error` with `name`, `status`, and non-sensitive diagnostic data.
- **[PATTERN]** Limit the concurrency of uploads, bulk fetches, and heavy tasks with a pool of N async workers (4-6 for the same origin), never `Promise.all` over hundreds of simultaneous requests; the pool accepts a `signal` and returns results in `PromiseSettledResult` format.
- **[PATTERN]** Use `Promise.withResolvers()` (ES2024: Chrome 119+, Firefox 121+, Safari 17.4+) for externally resolved promises (worker handshake, waiting for an event) instead of hand-captured `let resolve` variables.
- **[MANDATORY]** Register `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', handler)` and `window.addEventListener('error', handler)` in the composition root to send escaped rejections to telemetry with `navigator.sendBeacon()`; they are a safety net and do not replace local handling.
- **[SECURITY]** Before sending errors to telemetry, strip tokens, `Authorization` headers, query strings with personal data, and PII from `message` and `cause`; always-present timeouts prevent hanging requests that exhaust connections and memory.
- **[TESTING]** Test retry, backoff, and timeouts with `vi.useFakeTimers()` and `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)`; `Math.random` and the wait function are injectable or mocked (`vi.spyOn(Math, 'random').mockReturnValue(0.5)`) to make the jitter deterministic; the abort path has a dedicated test (no DOM update after `abort()`).
- **[CONFIGURATION]** ESLint: `no-async-promise-executor`, `prefer-promise-reject-errors`, `require-atomic-updates`, `no-await-in-loop` as `warn` (can be disabled line by line with a justified comment when sequential execution is intentional); with type-aware linting on `checkJs`, enable `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-async-concurrency.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 4. DOM Security and XSS Prevention (`js-dom-xss-security`)

*Scope:* Client-side security against DOM XSS: textContent, DOMPurify, Trusted Types and CSP, no eval, URL validation, safe postMessage, noopener, tokens out of localStorage, prototype pollution, and SRI. Use it when code writes to the DOM, navigates to dynamic URLs, or communicates between windows.

- **[MANDATORY]** Treat as untrusted user input, API responses, `location.hash`, `location.search`, `document.referrer`, `window.name`, `postMessage` messages, and data read from storage: they are DOM XSS sources just like a form field.
- **[MANDATORY]** Insert text only with `textContent`, `document.createTextNode()`, `element.append('string')`, or typed properties (`input.value`, `el.dataset.x`); `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML()`, `document.write()`, and `Range.createContextualFragment()` with untrusted data are forbidden.
- **[MANDATORY]** Untrusted rich HTML (comments, rendered markdown, CMS content) sanitized with DOMPurify and an explicit allowlist: `DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty, { ALLOWED_TAGS: ['p', 'strong', 'em', 'a'], ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href'] })`, adding `RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE: true` when Trusted Types are active; DOMPurify must be kept up to date because bypasses are fixed frequently.
- **[PATTERN]** Native Sanitizer API (`element.setHTML(dirty)`): partial and recent support, not available in all browsers; use it only behind the feature detection `'setHTML' in Element.prototype` with a fallback to DOMPurify.
- **[SECURITY]** Enable Trusted Types with the CSP `require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types app-html dompurify` and create named policies with `trustedTypes.createPolicy('app-html', { createHTML: (s) => DOMPurify.sanitize(s) })`; support is complete in Chromium (83+) but not in all other browsers: feature-detect with `window.trustedTypes?.createPolicy` and apply sanitization everywhere anyway.
- **[SECURITY]** Strict CSP without `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts: `script-src 'nonce-{random}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'`, with a random nonce generated by the server on every response.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `eval()`, `new Function()`, `setTimeout('code')`/`setInterval('code')` with strings, `script.textContent = data`, dynamically generated inline handlers (`onclick="deleteItem(42)"`), and `javascript:` URLs; enable the ESLint rules `no-eval`, `no-implied-eval`, `no-new-func`, and `no-script-url` at `error` level.
- **[MANDATORY]** Validate every dynamic URL before assigning it to `href`, `src`, `action`, `formAction`, `location`, or `window.open()`: parse with `new URL(raw, location.origin)` (preceded by `URL.canParse()`: Chrome 120+, Firefox 115+, Safari 17+) and an allowlist `new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:'])` on `url.protocol`; regexes and `startsWith('javascript:')` are forbidden, as they can be bypassed with uppercase letters, spaces, or leading tabs.
- **[SECURITY]** Post-login redirects and `returnUrl` parameters are accepted only if `new URL(raw, location.origin).origin === location.origin`, to prevent open redirects to phishing domains.
- **[MANDATORY]** `postMessage` always with an explicit `targetOrigin` (`frame.contentWindow.postMessage(data, 'https://pay.example.com')`), never `'*'`; on receipt compare `event.origin` with `===` against an allowlist (never `includes()`, `startsWith()`, or `endsWith()`), verify `event.source`, and validate the shape and types of `event.data` before using it.
- **[SECURITY]** Links to external origins with `target="_blank"` always accompanied by `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; programmatic opening with `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Session tokens, JWTs, and refresh tokens in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, or IndexedDB, readable by any injected script: use `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` cookies set by the server (BFF pattern); if an access token must live in the client, only in memory and short-lived.
- **[SECURITY]** Defense against prototype pollution: when merging or assigning dynamic keys from untrusted JSON, discard `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`; use `Map` or `Object.create(null)` for dictionaries with arbitrary keys, `Object.hasOwn()` for lookups, and an allowlist of keys and values for configurations.
- **[SECURITY]** Scripts and stylesheets from CDNs with Subresource Integrity and a pinned version: an `integrity` attribute with a base64 `sha384` hash and `crossorigin="anonymous"`, hash generated with `openssl dgst -sha384 -binary purify.min.js | openssl base64 -A`; never URLs with `@latest` or floating versions.
- **[PATTERN]** Dynamic attributes set with `setAttribute()` only for allowlisted names: never `on*`, `style`, `srcdoc`, or `formaction` attributes, nor `href`/`src` without URL validation.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Home-made mini template engines that concatenate HTML strings, `element.innerHTML = marked.parse(markdown)` without sanitization, jQuery `$(userInput)` or `$(el).html(data)`.
- **[TESTING]** Regression tests with real payloads: `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`, `<svg onload=alert(1)>`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `JaVaScRiPt:alert(1)`, `{"__proto__":{"isAdmin":true}}`; assert that no generated `img` or `svg` nodes exist, that `href` is not set, and that `({}).isAdmin` remains `undefined`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Introduce the CSP first as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` with a `report-to` directive to discover existing sinks, then switch to enforcement; in development with Vite set the headers via `server.headers` in `vite.config.js`.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-dom-xss-security.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 5. Web Components with Custom Elements and Shadow DOM (`js-web-components`)

*Scope:* Native Web Components: Custom Elements with lifecycle and cleanup, Shadow DOM with adoptedStyleSheets, attribute and property reflection, observedAttributes, composed CustomEvents, slots, ElementInternals for forms and accessibility. Use it to create or modify UI components without a framework.

- **[MANDATORY]** Custom element name with a hyphen and a project prefix (`acme-date-picker`; a name without a hyphen makes `customElements.define()` throw a `SyntaxError`); idempotent registration with `if (!customElements.get(name)) customElements.define(name, Ctor)`; one component per folder in `src/components/<name>/<name>.js`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Customized built-in elements (`class extends HTMLButtonElement` with `is="acme-button"`), not supported by Safari: always extend `HTMLElement` and use native elements inside the shadow root.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** In the `constructor`, reading or setting the host's attributes and children, running `fetch`, starting timers, or registering listeners on `window`/`document`: the specification forbids adding attributes or children (with `document.createElement()` the browser throws `NotSupportedError`); only `super()`, `attachShadow()`, `attachInternals()`, and building the internal structure of the shadow root are allowed.
- **[MANDATORY]** `connectedCallback` performs setup (global listeners, observers, fetches, timers) and `disconnectedCallback` the symmetric cleanup: create an `AbortController` on connection, pass `{ signal }` to every `addEventListener`, and call `abort()` on disconnection; `connectedCallback` runs again on every move within the DOM, so setup must be idempotent.
- **[PATTERN]** Shadow DOM with `this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })` and styles via a constructable `CSSStyleSheet` created once at module level with `sheet.replaceSync(css)` and assigned with `shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets = [sheet]` (Chrome 73+, Firefox 101+, Safari 16.4+): a single parse for all instances.
- **[PATTERN]** Attributes for declarative configuration (strings, booleans by presence), properties for the programmatic API and complex data; primitive properties reflect to the attribute (`set disabled(v) { this.toggleAttribute('disabled', Boolean(v)); }`); a boolean attribute is true if present, never `disabled="false"`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Observe attributes with the static field `static observedAttributes = ['value', 'max']` and handle them in `attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue)` with an early return if `oldValue === newValue`; the update touches only the affected nodes, never a full re-render of the shadow root.
- **[PATTERN]** Properties set on the instance before the upgrade (component defined with `import()` after parsing): in `connectedCallback` check `Object.hasOwn(this, 'value')`, save the value, delete the own property, and reassign it, so it goes through the class setter.
- **[PATTERN]** Public events as `new CustomEvent('acme-change', { detail: { value }, bubbles: true, composed: true })` dispatched on the host: `composed: true` lets the event cross shadow boundaries when the component is nested in another component's shadow root; prefixed kebab-case names so they do not collide with native events (`change`, `toggle`, `select`); serializable `detail`.
- **[PATTERN]** Consumer content projected with `<slot>` and named slots (`<slot name="header">`); react to changes with the `slotchange` event by reading `slot.assignedElements({ flatten: true })`; style projected content with `::slotted()` and allow external customization via CSS custom properties (`var(--acme-accent, #0a66c2)`) and `::part()`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Custom form controls as form-associated custom elements: `static formAssociated = true`, `this.#internals = this.attachInternals()`, `internals.setFormValue(value)`, `internals.setValidity(flags, message, anchor)`, and the callbacks `formResetCallback`, `formDisabledCallback`, `formStateRestoreCallback` (Chrome 77+, Firefox 98+, Safari 16.4+); helper `<input type="hidden">` elements in the light DOM are forbidden.
- **[MANDATORY]** Accessibility: role and states via `ElementInternals` (`internals.role = 'switch'`, `internals.ariaChecked = 'true'`, supported in recent evergreen browsers) or explicit ARIA attributes; native internal controls (`<button type="button">`) or `tabindex="0"` with Enter and Space handling; `attachShadow({ mode: 'open', delegatesFocus: true })` when focus must reach the internal control; `:focus-visible` always styled.
- **[SECURITY]** No `innerHTML` with attribute or property values during rendering: the shadow root structure is static (created with `createElement()` or cloned from a constant `<template>`) and dynamic values go through `textContent` or `setAttribute()`; Shadow DOM isolates styles but is not a security boundary, not even with `mode: 'closed'`.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Batch multiple attribute or property changes in the same task into a single update with `queueMicrotask()` and an `#updateScheduled` flag, or with `requestAnimationFrame` for purely visual updates.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Define heavy components only when needed: `import('./acme-chart.js')` on visibility or interaction and `await customElements.whenDefined('acme-chart')`; hide not-yet-defined elements with `acme-chart:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }` to avoid a flash of unstyled content.
- **[TESTING]** Test components through their public API (attributes, properties, events, accessible roles) in happy-dom or jsdom, querying the shadow root with @testing-library/dom's `within(el.shadowRoot)`; for `ElementInternals`, form validation, and real layout use Vitest Browser Mode with Playwright, because simulated environments support them only partially.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Document the public API with the JSDoc tags `@attr`, `@fires`, `@slot`, `@csspart`, and `@cssprop` on the class and generate `custom-elements.json` with `@custom-elements-manifest/analyzer` for IDEs and documentation.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-web-components.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 6. Memory Management and Leak Prevention (`js-memory-management`)

*Scope:* Preventing and diagnosing memory leaks in vanilla JavaScript: listeners removed with AbortSignal, timer and observer cleanup, WeakMap/WeakRef, detached DOM, closures, bounded LRU caches, FinalizationRegistry, and DevTools heap snapshots. Use it for long-lived views, components, and caches.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Every mounted view, component, or feature has an explicit lifecycle: `mount()` returns `{ destroy() }` or accepts a `signal: AbortSignal`; the router calls the cleanup of the outgoing view before mounting the next one.
- **[MANDATORY]** Register listeners with `addEventListener(type, handler, { signal })` (Chrome 90+, Firefox 86+, Safari 15+) and remove them all with a single `controller.abort()`; for view hierarchies use derived signals with `AbortSignal.any([appSignal, viewController.signal])`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `removeEventListener` with a function different from the registered one (inline arrow, regenerated `this.onClick.bind(this)`) or with a different `capture` option: it removes nothing and the listener keeps retaining closures and nodes.
- **[MANDATORY]** Timers are always cancelable: save the `setTimeout`/`setInterval` id and call `clearTimeout`/`clearInterval` in the cleanup; for polling use a recursive `setTimeout` that stops on `signal.aborted` and pauses when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`; use `cancelAnimationFrame()` for `requestAnimationFrame` loops.
- **[MANDATORY]** Release resources with the explicit APIs: `disconnect()` for `IntersectionObserver`, `ResizeObserver`, `MutationObserver`, and `PerformanceObserver` (`unobserve(el)` for a single target), `worker.terminate()`, `close()` for `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `BroadcastChannel`, and `MessagePort`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Keeping references to nodes removed from the DOM in arrays, `Map`s, `Set`s, caches, closures, or properties of long-lived objects (detached DOM tree): a single reference to a child node retains the entire subtree; store identifiers (`data-id`) instead of nodes.
- **[PATTERN]** Data associated with DOM nodes or with objects whose lifecycle you do not control goes in a `WeakMap<Element, Data>` or `WeakSet`: the entry is collected together with the key; expando properties (`el.__order = order`) and `Map`s keyed by nodes are forbidden.
- **[PATTERN]** `WeakRef` (Chrome 84+, Firefox 79+, Safari 14.1+) only for optional caches of large, rebuildable objects, checking `ref.deref()` on every access; the garbage collector is non-deterministic, so never use it for logic that must behave predictably.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `FinalizationRegistry` for mandatory cleanup (removing listeners, closing connections, saving data): the specification does not guarantee that callbacks will ever be invoked; use it only for diagnostics, for example to report undestroyed instances in development.
- **[PATTERN]** Long-lived closures (listeners, intervals, observer callbacks) capture only the values they need (`const { sku } = product`) and not the entire payload; in V8 closures created in the same scope share the context, so a large variable used by one closure stays alive as long as any other closure from that scope is alive.
- **[MANDATORY]** Every in-memory cache is bounded: an LRU on `Map` (update recency with `delete` + `set`, evict the first keys of `map.keys()` beyond `maxEntries`) with a TTL; `const cache = {}` objects that grow for the entire session are forbidden.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Structures that grow without bound: event logs, undo history, retry queues, analytics buffers; impose a limit (e.g. 100 entries) discarding the oldest; no `console.log` of large objects in production, because with DevTools open they stay referenced.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Release binary resources: `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` after `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` (for example after `await img.decode()`), `ImageBitmap.close()`, `VideoFrame.close()`; transfer `ArrayBuffer`s to workers with `postMessage(buffer, [buffer])` instead of cloning them.
- **[SECURITY]** On logout clear caches, stores, and structures that hold personal data or tokens (`cache.clear()`, store reset, `abort()` of in-flight requests), so the data does not remain reachable in the tab's heap.
- **[TESTING]** Diagnose with Chrome DevTools > Memory: take a baseline heap snapshot, repeat the mount/unmount cycle N times, force garbage collection (trash-can icon), and take a new snapshot; in the Comparison view look for growing objects, filter by `Detached` to find `Detached HTMLDivElement`s, and follow the chain in the Retainers panel.
- **[TESTING]** Automated cleanup tests: after `destroy()` a dispatched event must not invoke the handler (`expect(handler).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`), with fake timers `vi.getTimerCount()` must be 0, and mocked observers must have received `disconnect()`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** For critical flows (SPA navigation, opening and closing modals) run MemLab scenarios in CI (`npx memlab run --scenario scenario.js`) that detect detached DOM and objects growing across iterations; `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` is available only in cross-origin isolated contexts on Chromium.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-memory-management.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 7. Testing with Vitest and Testing Library (`js-testing-vitest`)

*Scope:* Testing vanilla JavaScript with Vitest: jsdom/happy-dom, @testing-library/dom with role queries, fake timers, fetch mocking with MSW or vi.spyOn, pure logic without the DOM, Arrange-Act-Assert, cleanup, and coverage thresholds. Use it when writing or fixing unit and integration tests.

- **[CONFIGURATION]** `vitest.config.js` with `defineConfig` imported from `vitest/config`: `environment: 'happy-dom'` (faster) or `'jsdom'` (more faithful for forms and CSS), `setupFiles: ['./test/setup.js']`, `include: ['src/**/*.test.js']`, `restoreMocks: true`, and `unstubGlobals: true`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Coverage with `@vitest/coverage-v8`: `coverage: { provider: 'v8', include: ['src/**/*.js'], exclude: ['src/**/*.test.js', 'src/main.js'], thresholds: { lines: 80, functions: 80, statements: 80, branches: 75 } }`; CI runs `npx vitest run --coverage` and fails below the threshold.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** In `test/setup.js` import `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` for the matchers `toBeInTheDocument()`, `toBeEnabled()`, `toHaveAccessibleName()`, and `toHaveTextContent()`; files that test only pure logic declare `// @vitest-environment node` at the top.
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Tests co-located next to the module (`cart-store.js` and `cart-store.test.js`); `describe` with the name of the public unit and `it` describing in English the expected behavior and the condition (`it('returns the total in cents when the cart contains discounts')`).
- **[MANDATORY]** Arrange-Act-Assert structure with the three phases separated by a blank line or comment, a single behavior per `it`, no conditional logic or loops in tests; table cases use `it.each(cases)` with an explicit table of inputs and expected outputs.
- **[PATTERN]** Pure logic (reducers, selectors, formatters, validators) tested without DOM or mocks: explicit inputs and output checked with `toEqual`/`toBe`; it is the level with the most tests and the fastest in the pyramid.
- **[MANDATORY]** @testing-library/dom queries in priority order: `getByRole(container, 'button', { name: 'Save' })`, then `getByLabelText`, `getByText`, and only as a last resort `getByTestId`; `querySelector` with CSS classes or structural selectors (`tr:nth-child(2) td`) is forbidden.
- **[MANDATORY]** User interactions with `@testing-library/user-event` (`const user = userEvent.setup(); await user.type(input, 'shoes')`) instead of manual `dispatchEvent` or `fireEvent`, which do not reproduce focus, the `keydown`/`keyup` sequence, and `input`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Testing private details: `#private` fields, `_internal` properties, non-exported functions, the number of calls to internal helpers, or DOM structure the user cannot perceive; snapshots of the entire `document.body.innerHTML` as the only assertion are forbidden.
- **[PATTERN]** Controlled time: `vi.useFakeTimers()` in `beforeEach` and `vi.useRealTimers()` in `afterEach`; `vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms)` for synchronous code and `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)` when there are promises between timers (debounce with fetch, retry with backoff); with user-event use `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Real waits such as `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))`; with Vitest fake timers do not use Testing Library's `findBy*` or `waitFor`, which only recognize Jest's fake timers and can hang: after advancing time use synchronous `getBy*` queries or `vi.waitFor()`.
- **[PATTERN]** Network mocks in unit tests: a fake `fetchFn` injected via factory or `vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(new Response(JSON.stringify(data), { status: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }))` with real `Response` objects; never fake objects with only a `json()` method and no `ok`, `status`, and `headers`.
- **[PATTERN]** Integration tests with MSW: `setupServer(http.get('https://api.acme.test/cart', () => HttpResponse.json(data)))` imported from `msw/node`, `server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' })` in `beforeAll`, `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach`, `server.close()` in `afterAll`, and per-test overrides with `server.use()`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Cleanup in `afterEach`: `document.body.replaceChildren()` (@testing-library/dom does not clean up automatically), `abort()` of mounted components' controllers, `vi.restoreAllMocks()` and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` if not configured globally; every test must pass on its own and in random order (`sequence: { shuffle: true }`).
- **[TESTING]** Error and cancellation paths verified explicitly: `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('Loading orders failed')`, `await expect(promise).rejects.toHaveProperty('cause', expect.any(HttpError))` and, after `controller.abort()`, no DOM updates; `expect.assertions(n)` when assertions live in async callbacks.
- **[SECURITY]** XSS regression tests on views that render external data: with the input `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` verify `expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull()` and that the text appears literally with `getByText('<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>')`.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** A fast suite: pure logic in the `node` environment, simulated DOM only where needed, Vitest Browser Mode with Playwright reserved for cases that require real layout, `ElementInternals`, or APIs not implemented by jsdom/happy-dom; no real network calls in any test.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Committed `.only` and `.skip`: enable `@vitest/eslint-plugin` with the rules `vitest/no-focused-tests` and `vitest/no-disabled-tests` in the flat config for `**/*.test.js` files.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/js-testing-vitest.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.
